key_insight: Surrogate-guided reinforcement learning enriches perovskite recipe shortlists with candidates near high-performing measured devices, without establishing experimental performance.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help prioritize solar-cell recipes for fabrication across large composition, device-layer, and processing design spaces.
method: Use a frozen Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) to guide recipe generation.
Compare three learned policies with six baselines using 3,000 surrogate evaluations per run.
Assess candidate support through neighborhoods of 890 measured reference devices.
evidence_signal: In top-100 shortlists, PPO and recurrent PPO achieved neighborhood-supported hit rates of 23% and 24%, versus 2.9% for Pure Random and 10% for the strongest baselines on this metric.
watch_item: Support is similarity-sensitive: composition-family matches among 9,000 recipes fell from 65.4% at similarity 0.80 to 11.7% at 0.90; experimental validation, seed robustness, and matched-budget advantage remain unestablished.
paper_title: Enrichment-Oriented Virtual Screening of Perovskite Solar Cells through Reinforcement Learning
